observed_gap: ENTRY_CANONICALIZATION_CONTRACT requires duplicate JSON member rejection before ordinary Mapping construction can erase duplicate names, but the retained Typed Entry module exposed only Mapping-based admit_entry(). Therefore a raw JSON object containing duplicate authority-relevant fields could be collapsed by an upstream permissive parser before typed admission observed the original structure.
hypothesis: A fail-closed raw-ingress parser using duplicate-preserving object-pair parsing is required before typed EntityOS/HCU Entry admission if raw JSON is accepted at any external boundary.
strongest_counterhypothesis: Every real caller may already receive a trusted duplicate-rejecting Mapping from an upstream parser, making a second raw parser unnecessary.
counterhypothesis_status: UNPROVEN: no exact admitted upstream parser/runtime boundary was executable or evidenced in this organ; therefore the source contract cannot assume duplicate rejection occurred before Mapping construction.

primary_external_evidence.relevance: JCS requires I-JSON-compatible input and invariant canonical representation for cryptographic hashing; duplicate object property names are not admitted. This supports rejecting duplicate members before causal hash identity is minted, but does not by itself prove current runtime wiring.
